intended_object: The maximal ideal of the point v of the affine space attached to V: the kernel of evaluation at v, Sym_k(V*) → k, i.e. the polynomial functions on V that vanish at v. Inferred from the docstring, the name, and the lemmas after it (`_isMaximal`, `symmetricAlgebraAffineCoordinatePoint`, and the comparison with MvPolynomial evaluation points).
explanation: The body is the kernel of `SymmetricAlgebra.lift (Module.Dual.eval k V v)`. This is the k-algebra map Sym(V*) → k that sends each generator φ ∈ V* to φ(v), so it is evaluation of polynomial functions at v. Its kernel is the ideal of polynomial functions vanishing at v, which is exactly the intended object. Through a dual basis, the library proves that this ideal matches the usual ideal (X_i − v_i) in MvPolynomial (`mvPolynomialAffineCoordinatePoint_comap_equivMvPolynomial`). The ideal is maximal because evaluation is surjective onto k. Taking k to be a field is the standard setting for the affine space of a vector space, and the library uses that setting to study closed points (the Nullstellensatz part also assumes k algebraically closed). Mathlib has no basis-free counterpart: the closest notions are kernels of `MvPolynomial.aeval` and `PrimeSpectrum.vanishingIdeal`, and neither is this intrinsic construction on the symmetric algebra of the dual.
